ap_biology-f01.title: Analyzing an energy bar graph

stimulus.description: Energy available at three trophic levels of an ecosystem (primary and secondary refer to primary and secondary consumers)

data.title: Energy available at three trophic levels

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the percent of the energy at the producer level that is transferred to the primary consumers.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct percent transfer (answer)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Explain where the energy that is not transferred to the next trophic level goes.
parts.model_answer: Much of the energy is lost as heat during cellular respiration and is used for the organism's own metabolism, and some is not eaten or is in waste.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that most of the energy is lost as heat or used in the organism's metabolism
required_elements: Most of the energy is lost as heat from metabolic processes or used by the organisms, and some remains in uneaten parts or waste
alt_solutions: released as heat during cellular respiration
used by the organism for its own life processes or left in waste and dead material
common_errors: says the energy is transferred to the producers
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Using the same percent of energy transferred, determine the energy available to tertiary consumers, and represent it by adding a fourth bar to the bar chart.
parts.model_answer: 100 x 10/100 = 10 kcal per year, shown as a fourth bar much shorter than the third bar.

rubric_rows.criterion: Gives the correct energy for the next level and draws a bar of the correct relative height (value)
common_errors: uses the wrong values from the table or an incorrect formula
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain how the pattern shown by the bar chart is consistent with the statement that energy flows through ecosystems while matter is recycled.
parts.model_answer: Energy decreases at each level as heat is lost and cannot be reused by producers, so ecosystems need a constant input of energy, while the matter in the molecules is recycled by decomposers.

rubric_rows.criterion: Connects the decrease in energy at each level to a one-way flow with an outside source, while matter is recycled
required_elements: Energy is lost as heat at each level and not reused, so an ecosystem needs constant energy input, while matter is recycled
alt_solutions: energy is lost as heat so a continuous energy input is required
decomposers return matter to producers but heat cannot be recaptured
common_errors: says energy is recycled by decomposers
says matter is lost from ecosystems at each level
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase.
